title: Janus: workload profiling and safe batching operator for continuous rollout
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement 'Janus', a production-safe operator that continuously profiles inference workloads and recommends + applies batching and caching parameter bundles with automated safety checks and rollback. Goals: (1) produce per-customer and per-route workload fingerprints, (2) synthesize conservative batching/caching parameter bundles (batch_size, max_latency_target_ms, kv_cache_ttl_ms, prefix_cache_enabled, pooling_policy), (3) run an automated canary rollout that monitors latency/cost/error signals and supports immediate automatic rollback when thresholds are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: Janus produces workload fingerprints for 95% of active routes within 48h of enablement

A generated parameter bundle can be applied to a canary subset (config flag) and will automatically halt or rollback if p95 latency increases > 5% compared to baseline or error-rate increases by > 0.5%
Offline replay harness exists to simulate the expected cost/save delta for a given bundle with <10% error vs production observed after rollout
Operator publishes human-readable rationale for each recommendation (dominant request shapes, token distribution, caching hit-rate projection)
Safe-apply requires feature-flag + leader-election and writes change to central config store with audit entry and optional manual approval depending on confidence score
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Kickoff meeting. Scoped initial MVP to host routes + dedicated test cluster. Assigned Diego (eng) and Maya (PM).

2026-02-25: Profiling prototype completed: lightweight sampler in front of runtime emits request shape histograms (seq_len, prefix_len, call_pattern) stored to telemetry.fast_profiles. Need to reduce telemetry cardinality.
2026-03-02: Heuristics draft: confidence score derived from sample volume, traffic stability, and historical rollout variance. Discussed leaf heuristics (latency headroom, cacheability index).
notes: Key trade-offs: conservative defaults vs capture of cost upside. We bias towards conservative bundles for first 3 rollouts; increase aggressiveness as confidence grows.
We must coordinate with autoscaler team: batch_size increases change GPU scheduling behavior and can temporarily raise queueing latency. Add a mandatory autoscaler check before bundle apply.
Prefix cache TTL interacts with privacy policies for some customers; add per-customer opt-out flag and a validation step in the apply flow.
safety_checks: cost delta threshold: if tokens/sec cost increases > 2% for > 30m then halt
minimal sample volume: >= 10k requests observed in the last 24h for route to be eligible for auto-apply
rollout_plan: Canary schedule: 1% traffic for 30m -> 5% for 2h -> 20% for 6h -> 50% for 12h -> 100%
At each stage Janus evaluates safety checks and computes rollback recommendation. If any check trips, operator reverts to previous config and creates an incident ticket.
Fallback: if canary fails, route is pinned to baseline model variant for 24h and engineering notifies the owning team.
offline_harness: Replay harness implemented at runtime/test-replay - replays sampled traces against proposed bundles to compute expected p95 and cost delta
Current gap: harness does not model KV cache cold-start accurately; follow-up task to capture warmup curves (ENG-389221)
followups: Expose human-in-the-loop UI in Console for bundle preview + forced-apply
Extend heuristic set with ML-based bandit once we have 90+ routes profiled
